title: W002 initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke
description:
W002 workset epic: Initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke.

Goal: drive the first executable OxForms slice from plan to evidence. This workset proves the architecture direction by having a VBA app project load the OxForms VBA library, create a smoke-only OxForms form-like object, let the library create a host-injected OxForms smoke canvas through OxVba's portable COM-like projection, call a minimal FillRect display-list command through that object, have an OxVba adapter map that call into the OxForms PAL core, have Rust render it headlessly with stable diagnostics, and have a Windows visible smoke path paint the same command.

Read first:
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md, especially Purpose, Non-goals, Architecture Slice, Closure Condition, Verification Shape, Risks And Controls, and the oxforms-dwm.7 through oxforms-dwm.10 repair notes.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D2, D8, D9, D10, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, 9, 10.2, and the W002 bootstrap slice in section 11.
- docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md section OxVba Development Baseline for pinned dependency policy.
- docs/evidence/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md Structural Coupling Repairs.

Non-goals for the whole epic: do not implement full UserForm.Show, .frm/.frx parsing, intrinsic controls, text metrics, input routing, timers, clipboard, image decode, or MSForms parity claims. The smoke API is temporary and must be named/treated as smoke-only.
design:
Execution model:
1. oxforms-dwm.1 finishes the self-contained bead/workset plan.
2. oxforms-dwm.2 scaffolds the Rust/VBA workspace using the pinned OxVba dependency policy.
3. oxforms-dwm.3 implements DisplayList/FillRect and a deterministic headless renderer.
4. oxforms-dwm.4 initially proved VBA execution with a weak Debug.Print trace path.
5. oxforms-dwm.5 adds a Windows visible smoke path from the same display list.
6. oxforms-dwm.6 records evidence and closes the first pass.
7. oxforms-dwm.7 repairs the coupling: VBA uses CreateObject("OxForms.SmokeCanvas"), calls CreateSurface/FillRect/Flush, and Rust renders on Flush.
8. oxforms-dwm.8 repairs the ownership direction: OxVba loads an app .basproj plus referenced OxForms.basproj; the app creates an OxForms smoke form; the OxForms library owns the PAL canvas bridge.
9. oxforms-dwm.9 repairs the adapter naming: the Rust module is named oxvba_pal_adapter so it reads as an OxVba-facing PAL adapter, not as Rust hosting VBA.
10. oxforms-dwm.10 repairs the crate layering: oxforms-pal is host/runtime independent, while oxforms-oxvba-adapter owns PortableDispatch, Variant marshalling, projection registration, and the OxVba smoke test.

Headless rendering is the automated oracle; visible Windows rendering is important but should not become a flaky CI gate. The repaired OxVba proof is app project -> OxForms VBA library -> OxVba adapter -> PAL core renderer, not stdout/string parsing and not OxVba embedded in the PAL core.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic is complete only when:
- oxforms-dwm.2 through oxforms-dwm.10 are closed with their acceptance checks satisfied.
- The Rust PAL renders a FillRect display list headlessly with stable checked diagnostics/hash.
- The OxVba-driven VBA smoke loads RectangleSmokeApp.basproj plus referenced OxForms.basproj, and the app does not directly create OxForms.SmokeCanvas.
- The OxForms VBA library creates/accesses a host-injected OxForms.SmokeCanvas and reaches the Rust PAL core through the OxVba adapter by calling CreateSurface, FillRect, and Flush.
- The VBA smoke proof does not rely on Debug.Print/stdout-style trace strings as the coupling mechanism.
- oxforms-pal contains no OxVba dependencies; OxVba-specific PortableDispatch/Variant marshalling lives in oxforms-oxvba-adapter.
- The Windows visible smoke exists and is verified on Windows, or a concrete blocker/follow-up bead records why it could not be verified.
- Evidence records commands, artifacts, hashes, platform notes, and fresh-eyes review outcome.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md and docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md accurately describe final status.
notes:
Dependency: W002 depends on oxforms-rzk / W001 repo bootstrap. Do not start implementation beads until W001 and oxforms-dwm.1 are closed.

Review rule for every child bead: At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.
close_reason: Reclosed W002 after oxforms-dwm.10: smoke proves app -> OxForms VBA library -> OxVba adapter -> OxForms PAL core, with oxforms-pal independent of OxVba.

title: Split OxVba adapter from PAL core
description:
Repair bead: split the W002 OxVba smoke adapter out of oxforms-pal so the PAL core is OxVba-independent.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md, especially the oxforms-dwm.8 and oxforms-dwm.9 repair notes.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D2, D8, D9, D10 and sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, and 9.
- docs/evidence/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md Structural Coupling Repairs.
- crates/oxforms-pal/Cargo.toml, crates/oxforms-pal/src/lib.rs, and the current OxVba rectangle smoke test.

Scope:
- Make crates/oxforms-pal the OxVba-independent PAL core: no oxvba-* dependencies, no PortableDispatch/PortableComProjection/Variant references, and no default feature that pulls OxVba in.
- Add a focused OxVba adapter crate, expected crates/oxforms-oxvba-adapter, that depends on oxforms-pal and owns PortableDispatch, PortableComProjection registration, Variant marshalling, and the W002 SmokeCanvas ProgID.
- Move the app -> OxForms VBA library -> Rust PAL smoke integration test into the adapter crate.
- Preserve W002 behavior and evidence: app basproj references OxForms.basproj, OxForms creates OxForms.SmokeCanvas internally, Rust records the display list and render diagnostics.
- Update docs/evidence/register/source references as needed so the architecture is explicit: PAL core is host/runtime independent; OxVba integration is an adapter layer.

Non-goals:
- Do not expand the PAL command vocabulary beyond W002 FillRect.
- Do not change the VBA smoke API beyond what crate extraction requires.
- Do not add real UserForm.Show, .frm/.frx ingestion, intrinsic controls, or input/events.
- No sibling-repo edits.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:

- rg over crates/oxforms-pal finds no PortableDispatch, PortableComProjection, Variant, or oxvba_* adapter references except neutral docs/comments if intentionally justified.
- A dedicated OxVba adapter crate owns the W002 SmokeCanvas portable COM projection adapter and the OxVba rectangle smoke test.
- cargo test -p oxforms-pal --no-default-features passes, proving the PAL core builds without OxVba.
- cargo test -p oxforms-oxvba-adapter --test oxvba_rectangle_smoke -- --nocapture passes, proving the app -> OxForms library -> PAL adapter smoke still works.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, git diff --check, br dep cycles, and br ready --json pass.
- W002 docs/evidence/register clearly state the layering and remain smoke-only.
- Commit code/docs/evidence/bead state with this bead ID in the message.

Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.

title: Implement display-list core and headless rectangle renderer
description:
Implementation bead: implement the display-list core and deterministic headless rectangle renderer.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Architecture Slice items 1-2, Closure Condition items 1 and 5, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.4 Display Lists, 6.2 Contract Surface, and 10.2 Fidelity Strategy.
- The workspace scaffold from oxforms-dwm.2.

Scope:
- Define the first stable-enough smoke display-list data model: version, logical surface dimensions, Rect, Color with explicit byte order, DisplayCommand::FillRect, and DisplayList.
- Implement validation for obviously invalid rectangles/surfaces where useful for deterministic behavior.
- Implement a deterministic headless renderer that fills an in-memory buffer and returns RenderDiagnostics containing at least dimensions, command count, and a stable hash/checksum.
- Add focused tests that render a known small rectangle fixture and assert the diagnostic/hash. Prefer tests that are deterministic across Windows/non-Windows hosts.
- Add or update docs/evidence or a fixture manifest only if there is a real artifact to preserve at this stage.

Non-goals:
- No VBA/OxVba execution in this bead.
- No visible Windows window in this bead.
- No text, images, input, timers, system colors, or MSForms themed controls.
design:
Design notes:
- Keep W002 to FillRect only. Resist adding line/ellipse/text/image commands until a later bead/workset needs them.
- Use headless rendering as the automated oracle. The later Windows smoke must consume the same DisplayList rather than defining a parallel command path.
- If serialization is added, version it. If serialization is deferred, ensure the in-memory contract is still explicit enough for oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5 to share.
- Choose a hash/checksum that is stable and easy to recompute in tests; do not use nondeterministic timing or platform paint output as the core oracle.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Rust tests prove a known FillRect display list renders to the expected deterministic diagnostics/hash.
- The display-list and renderer API are documented enough in code/tests for oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5 to use without reinterpreting the plan.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace pass, unless a check is not yet applicable and the reason is documented with a follow-up bead.
- git diff --check, br dep cycles, and br ready --json pass.
- Commit code, tests, docs/evidence if any, and bead state with this bead ID in the message.

Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.

title: Repair W002 smoke to use host-injected PAL canvas
description:
Repair bead: replace the W002 OxVba rectangle smoke string-trace path with structural host-object coupling.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Architecture Slice items 3-4, Closure Condition item 2, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D2, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, and 9.
- docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md section OxVba Development Baseline.
- The current oxforms-pal renderer API, vba/smoke fixture, and OxVba smoke test.

Scope:
- Make the VBA smoke obtain an OxForms smoke canvas through the OxVba host-injection / COM-like projection path, e.g. CreateObject("OxForms.SmokeCanvas") or the nearest equivalent supported by the pinned OxVba baseline.
- Make VBA call real members on that object, such as CreateSurface, FillRect, and Flush, so Rust host object dispatch records the display list and Flush drives the headless renderer.
- Keep the API clearly smoke-only and scoped to W002; do not implement UserForm.Show, .frm/.frx loading, intrinsic controls, events, or MSForms parity.
- Remove or stop relying on Debug.Print/stdout-style command strings for the coupling proof.
- Update W002 docs/evidence/register wording so the closed workset no longer claims a text trace as sufficient coupling.

Non-goals:
- No visible Windows backend redesign; oxforms-dwm.5 remains the visible path.
- No sibling-repo edits. If OxVba lacks the needed projection surface, record a concrete blocker/handover instead of mutating ../OxVba.
design: Design intent: W002 should prove the architecture in spec decision D2: an injected host object with a flat, C-ABI-ready value surface. The smoke canvas is a test-only Rust host object projected through OxVba. VBA dispatches member calls into that object; the object builds a DisplayList; Flush invokes the same deterministic headless renderer used by the Rust fixture. This is intentionally COM-like host injection, not final MSForms API surface.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- A documented command/test executes vba/smoke/fixtures/rectangle_fillrect_smoke.bas through OxVba and creates/accesses a host-projected OxForms smoke canvas object.
- The VBA fixture calls object members such as CreateSurface, FillRect, and Flush; the Rust host object records the display list and Flush renders via oxforms-pal::render_headless.
- The test asserts the host-recorded display list and render diagnostics match w002_rectangle_fixture_display_list and w002_rectangle_fixture_diagnostics.
- Debug.Print/stdout-style trace strings are not the coupling mechanism for the W002 proof.
- W002 workset/evidence/register docs describe the repaired coupling and keep all smoke-only/non-parity caveats.

title: W003 Excel Forms oracle and Windows capture plumbing
description:
W003 workset epic: Excel Forms oracle and Windows capture plumbing.

Goal: create the first reproducible black-box oracle path against real Microsoft Forms running inside Excel/VBA, so future OxForms rendering work has a measured target instead of guessing. W003 should produce a tiny real Excel UserForm fixture, a Windows capture/discovery harness, durable artifacts, and the first comparison manifest that points from the Excel oracle toward OxForms outputs.

Read first:
- CHARTER.md sections 3 and 4 for compatibility-first and clean-room constraints.
- OPERATIONS.md sections 7 and 8 for evidence and handover expectations.
- docs/worksets/W003_excel_forms_oracle_capture.md once created, especially Purpose, Non-goals, Architecture Slice, Closure Condition, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/evidence/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md for the existing OxForms rectangle baseline.

Non-goals for W003: do not implement .frm/.frx ingestion, UserForm.Show in OxForms, intrinsic controls in OxForms, pixel-exact matching, wasm/Tauri/web backends, broad UI Automation coverage, or Office-internal reverse engineering. W003 is an oracle/capture workset, not a renderer expansion.
design:
Execution model:
1. oxforms-fg9.3 writes and commits the W003 workset plan/register/bead graph.
2. oxforms-fg9.1 scaffolds an oracle harness and fixture/artifact layout.
3. oxforms-fg9.2 implements reusable Windows discovery/capture primitives.
4. oxforms-fg9.4 creates the first real Excel UserForm oracle fixture.
5. oxforms-fg9.5 combines the fixture and capture primitives to produce durable Excel oracle artifacts.
6. oxforms-fg9.6 defines the first oracle comparison artifact format and seeds a calibration comparison against existing OxForms outputs where possible.
7. oxforms-fg9.7 records evidence, reviews the whole workset, updates docs, and closes W003 only if objective closure conditions are met.

The graph intentionally puts the oracle before broader backend architecture. Other backends should be tracked as constraints, but not built, until the Excel/MSForms measuring stick exists.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic is complete only when:
- oxforms-fg9.1 through oxforms-fg9.7 are closed with their acceptance checks satisfied.
- A real Excel/VBA UserForm oracle fixture exists and is generated or opened reproducibly from repo-owned inputs.
- Windows capture/discovery records at least window identity, bounds, screenshot pixels, platform/Excel version notes, and useful logs for that fixture.
- Artifacts live under docs/evidence or another documented artifact path with stable manifests/checksums.
- A first comparison manifest describes how the Excel oracle output relates to the current OxForms W002 rectangle output or explicitly records why exact comparison is deferred.
- docs/worksets/W003_excel_forms_oracle_capture.md and docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md accurately describe final status.
- No committed artifact or process violates clean-room rules.
